read: [00:04] Amal: شو اليوم؟ .. [1:02:40] Amal: باي. (all 970 turns, lines 3-972)
coverage_note: Whole file read in order. Long English-only stretches (meta talk about the recorder 03:40-05:52; verb-pair explanation 17:06-18:06; usage discussion 46:08-48:13; causative-verb wrap-up 57:27-1:02:40). Latin transliteration on Medi's lines at 06:38-06:47 (date), 07:08-07:20 (clock), 19:39 (means ajik), 30:49 (albo), 48:20-48:31. ASR-garbled Amal fixes: 12:13 'بدائية' (read as وردية), 13:42 'فعلاً' (read as فعلين), 38:33 'أشياءي نوع الإل' (unreadable; Medi says he did not say ال - no row), 45:57 'بتنكسر'. Not written (S4/S5/self-fix): 03:11 جهزت->وجهّزت (shadda F3, twice), 05:58 الأربعاء->الخميس self-fix, 06:40 date order self-fix before her عشرة تسعة, 07:46 قربان for خربان (ق/خ), 15:02 أزعشتك (ش/ج), 20:57 متأكتي, 29:46 سكرتي self-fix, 33:41 سهوني (ص/س), 34:14 يسكر->اكسر self-fix (her 'K before S' = letter order), 35:17 كنا self-fix, 42:53-43:16 انكسرت letter-order fix, 52:52 اشي->إشي vowel, 44:18 اثنعش accepted as ممتاز. 'air conditioning' is used in English by both (07:39, 12:53, 48:29, 53:14) and is not on her sheet, so not tier 3. 09:13 'مهندس كهربجي' (redundant pairing) got an explanation, not a fix - no row. Medi turns counted = Medi lines containing Arabic script (366 of 615 Medi lines).

rows.why: He asked how the bride (عروس) was, meaning the wedding; she recast عرس and he repeated عروس again at 01:57.

Letter-order slip that lands on a different real verb (زعم = claimed) for عزمت (sheet: 'i invited | Ana 3azamet | أنا عزمت'); she recast it and Medi himself at 04:05 asked that it be marked wrong - borderline S4 root-letter slip.

rows.medi_said: Sa alaat ila nun-- ila tult.
rows.why: Clock time: he said talaat (three, masc/short form) for the time; she asked three or two, he fixed to intayn and she recast الساعة تنتين إلا تلت (feminine number after el-saa3a).
Answering 'how is the weather' he said 'weather very very' with no word for hot; sheet: 'it's hot | El-jaw shoab | الجو شوب'. B reading; ASR may have dropped the word.
rows.english: The weather is very hot today

rows.why: Known noun 'the weather' without el- (her own prompt was كيف الجو); she let it pass.

He used صلاح- (long a) for the form II verb صلّح 'fixed'; she recast صلحته. Borderline F2/F3 pronunciation, but he keeps the same wrong shape at 10:34 and 10:40, so it reads as the wrong form of the verb.

rows.medi_said: Is it raki? What was electricity?
rows.why: Didn't-know: he asked for the word for electricity and she supplied كهربا (sheet: 'electricity | Kahraba | كهربا').

rows.medi_said: مهندس-- Do you guys say مهندس كهرباء؟
rows.why: Profession idafa: the second noun takes el- (مهندس الكهربا); he left it bare and she recast.

rows.medi_said: I think is كراجي electrician, and then electrical engineering is...
rows.why: He turned her كهربجي into كراجي (a different word, garage/mechanic) and repeated it at 09:39 and 09:48; she recast كهربجي.

rows.medi_said: ما، ما يكون، كهربجي، هو مهندس
rows.why: Negating a noun predicate ('he is not a kahrabji, he is an engineer') with ما يكون instead of مش; she let it pass.
rows.english: He isn't an electrician, he's an engineer

rows.amal_said: You said صلح which is fix. You did wha-- did you wanna say he helped me?
rows.why: He used صلّح (fix) for 'help'; she asked whether he meant helped and he produced ساعدني (sheet: 'help | Saa3ed | ساعد'), which she confirmed at 11:10.

rows.amal_said: صلحني would be he fixed me. Like you, you were who's being fixed.
rows.why: She explained that the object on the verb (صلحني) means 'fixed me' while 'fixed for me' needs the preposition (صلح لي); low because the verb he actually meant (ساعدني) takes a direct object anyway.
Masculine colour adjective after the feminine noun بلوزة; her recast is transcribed as بدائية (almost certainly وردية) and she said صح when he repeated the feminine form at 12:14.
Wrong form of the verb 'stayed' (sheet: 'i stayed/kept | Ana dallait | أنا ضليت'); she did not understand ('what?') and supplied ضليت. Could also be read as B5 past ending.

rows.medi_said: اه، this is take Allah بيتي.
rows.why: He said 'stayed my house' with no preposition; she prompted 'bi or fi?' and he fixed to بي بيتي at 12:50.
'Because there is AC' rendered with يكون; ykoon is not how existence is stated here (في). She let it pass. 'air conditioning' is not on her sheet, so the English word is not an error.
Modifier before the noun (English order); she recast noun first, كلمة وحدة.

rows.medi_said: بس كلمة-- بس فعل، اه، تنين،
rows.why: 'Two verbs' needs the dual فعلين, not فعل + تنين; her recast is transcribed فعلاً, almost certainly فعلين.
'I annoyed you' = زعجتك (past 1sg + object -ك); his زعجتيك inserts an extra vowel/ending; she recast زعجتك (or أزعجتك) at 14:50-15:07.
Drill 'you got annoyed with me': he stalled in English and she supplied the past form انزعجتِ; he then produced انزعجتي at 15:52. Written as a didn't-know form, not a slip.
انزعج takes من; he trailed off with ما, she asked why ما, he fixed to مني (16:10) and gave انزعجتي مني at 16:22 ('Perfect').

rows.amal_said: بتحب نشوف الواجب أو الفعل اللي بعده؟
rows.why: He uses كم مرة ('how many times') to mean 'say it again / one more time'; sheet: 'one more time | Kaman marra | كمان مرة'. She just rephrased her question.
Second use of كم مرة for 'again' (sheet: 'one more time | Kaman marra | كمان مرة'); she repeated herself without fixing. He uses كمان مرة correctly at 57:03.
English calque 'one more' with أكتر; she recast كمان واحد (sheet: 'also / more / too | Kamaan | كمان').
Masculine participle for a female addressee; she asked 'inti or inta?' and he fixed to مزعوجة at 18:54.

rows.medi_said: And then باز is not بازوج, بازيجيني هدول اليوم.
rows.why: Plural subject 'many things' needs the plural verb بزعجوني; he used the singular; she recast twice and he acknowledged 'it's plural'.
rows.english: Many things annoy me these days

rows.why: Same plural-agreement slip repeated on his second attempt; she recast بزعجوني and he fixed at 20:33.
'These days' needs the plural أيام; he used the singular اليوم and she recast.

rows.medi_said: أيام. I even wrote أيام. هدول أيام.
rows.why: After the plural fix he said هدول أيام without el-; the noun after hadol keeps its el-. She let it pass.
'Are you sure THAT you didn't annoy him' needs إنو; he used اللي. She asked 'why illi?' (21:27) and said إنو مش اللي.
rows.english: Are you sure that you (pl) didn't annoy him?

rows.why: 'you (pl) didn't annoy HIM' is missing the object ending -ه on the verb; she moved to the illi problem and let this pass.

rows.amal_said: بس مبسوطة إذا ما بشوف هيك.
rows.why: After إذا ما she keeps the b- (إذا ما بشوف); he used the bare أشوفك; he repeated her form at 22:31. Her ruling here differs from the plain B3 drop, so filed under B3 as her exception.
rows.english: if I don't see you happy

rows.medi_said: Is it تكوني or just مبسوطة?
rows.amal_said: بس مبسوطة إذا ما بشوف هيك.
rows.why: Didn't-know: he asked whether the predicate needs تكوني; she said just مبسوطة, no بكون needed (22:42-22:57).
rows.english: if I don't see you (being) happy

rows.why: Negative command: he gave the positive imperative إنزعجي for 'don't be annoyed'; she prompted 'so don't be', he produced ما تنزعج (23:24) then ما تنزعجي (23:32) after her echo.
'With them' should be the preposition with its ending, منهم, not من + هم; she had prompted بعدين and let it pass (spacing may be ASR).
After مش قصدهم ('they didn't mean to') the verb drops its b-: يدايقوكي; he kept the b- and insisted 'أنا بعرف هيك' at 25:16. Pronouncing دايق as تاي is S4, not counted.
rows.english: They didn't mean to upset you

rows.medi_said: So I add his بزيء، بزياد،
rows.why: Wrong vowel shape for the present of زاد (I add = بزيد); she recast and he repeated بزيد.
Groping for 'I remove' he produced شول/فيل; she supplied بقيم (sheet: 'i remove / take away | Ba2eem | بقيم'); his later بعين/بعيم are ق-drop pronunciations of it (S4).

rows.medi_said: الـ أول الـ فعل، الـ أول الكلمة.
rows.why: Idafa: the first word never takes el- (أول الفعل / أول الكلمة); he put el- on both. She let it pass.
rows.english: the beginning of the verb / of the word

rows.why: بخسر is a different verb (I lose) for بكسر 'I break' (sheet: 'i break | Ana bakser | أنا بكسر'); she said 'close' and recast; he still said بخسر at 28:06-28:26 before switching. Could be argued as a خ/ك sound slip (S4).
3pl past needs -u (كسروا); he gave كسرت; her echo prompted him and he fixed at 28:47, confirmed 28:53.
In the present-tense drill (هم ...) he dropped the b-: يكسروا for بيكسروا; she let it pass.
'You keep breaking' - after إنتِ بتظلي the verb needs بت-: بتكسري; he said (ك)سري without it; she said she didn't hear the t and he fixed to بتكسري at 33:31.
MSA 2pl past ending -تم instead of Levantine -توا; she let it pass in the conjugation run.
'His cups' needs the plural كاسات + ه; he used the singular كاسته; she recast كساته.

For 'his cup' she recast كاسه; his كاسته keeps the -t- of كاسة before the possessive (sheet has 'cup | Kaasa | كاسة'), which is normally fine, so low - the transcript may have dropped her vowel (كاستو).
كاسة is feminine so the verb is انكسرت; he used the masculine; she recast and confirmed 'because it's female' at 41:00.
The subject is عمر (masc), so كان, not كانت, even though it is 'her' age; he pushed for كانت twice (43:36, 43:43) and she said لأ.
He said eleven for twelve (sheet: 'eleven | e7da3sh | إحداعش', 'twelve | tna3sh | تنعش'); she said 12 and إتناش (43:55).
Feminine form invented for the noun he knows (sheet: 'present tense | Mudaare3 | مضارع'); she recast مضارع; he still said المضارعة at 44:41.
Non-existent form for هو/هي (masc prefix + fem -i ending); she redirected to إنتو without fixing it.
إحنا of the un-verb needs بن + نكسر (بننكسر); he gave بنكسر (= we break); she moved on to usage. Her 45:57 line is garbled (بتنكسر).

rows.medi_said: Do I say for air condition?
rows.why: Didn't-know: he asked how to say 'my AC'; she supplied the تبعي construction (AC itself is not on her sheet, she keeps it in English). His echo تباين is pronunciation.

rows.amal_said: انكسر. Did it actually like break?
rows.why: انكسر is for physically shattering; for the AC 'stopped working' she wants خرب/خربان (49:05, 49:51 'my issue is with the verb itself... It's physical'); he conceded at 50:05.
rows.english: The AC broke (stopped working) from the heat

rows.why: 'I never broke anything' is past; he used present because he thought أبداً forces present; she asked بكسر أو كسرت, he fixed to ما كسرت (52:36) and she confirmed كسرت.

rows.amal_said: it? Do you wanna say because the, the air conditioning tired me?
rows.why: Letter-order slip turns تبعي (mine) into تعّبي ('tired me'); she read it as 'tired me out' and asked; he rephrased without it at 53:29. Borderline S4 but it changed the meaning and she flagged it.
Negate the verb with ما (ما نمت منيح), not مش before the adverb; she recast and he repeated at 53:54.

rows.medi_said: كل شيء تمام. Everything okay? Yeah? كل شيء تمام.
rows.why: MSA شيء for the Levantine شي she had just used (كلشي تمام؟; sheet: 'thing | Eshi | اشي'); she let it pass.

rows.medi_said: إن و-- إن. الف-الفعلات. الفعلات إن.
rows.why: Invented plural فعلات for فعل (sheet: 'verb – verbs | Fe3el | فعل'); she recast أفعال and he repeated الأفعال at 54:53. (Plural pattern -> tier 2 per brief; A9 territory.)
'I am annoyed' is the passive participle مزعوج; مزعج = annoying (both on her sheet as separate rows); she recast and asked what أنا مزعج means (56:52).

rows.medi_said: is it بزور بنكسر؟ بنكسر. أكسر. Okay.
rows.why: Naming the verb pair he gave the bare أكسر; she recast بكسر and بنكسر.
Replying to her يلا بشوفك with ما شوفتك (negated past, 'I didn't see you') for 'see you'; possibly ASR; she let it pass.
